title: Edited Docs Review Source Round-Trip Delivery
summary: rebuild edited review sources and import their complete staged source folder back to an exact scope or sub-scope
content_html:
Edited Docs Review Source Round-Trip Delivery

Status And Dependencies

Started as ERS-1 under Edited Docs Review Source Round-Trip. It replaces the former independent Docs Review Build delivery. Both prerequisites below are shipped. ERS-1.0 is complete; ERS-1.1 is the next bounded implementation checkpoint and has not started.

Build and edited-source-folder Import are one complete feature outcome. This delivery depended on both sub-scope Import-parity prerequisites:

  1. Sub-Scope Ordinary Document Import Delivery;
  2. Sub-Scope Returned Package Import Delivery.

The exact package-source Open in VS Code action and the synthetic Docs Review builder are already shipped. The prerequisites establish shared scope/sub-scope Import targets before this delivery adds another trusted collection format.

Complete Outcome

For a validated, import-capable review package from either a top-level scope or a configured sub-scope, the user can:

  1. edit package-local source/*.md files in VS Code;
  2. select Build in Docs Review to regenerate and inspect the complete retained preview;
  3. copy the package's complete source/ folder into Import staging;
  4. choose that folder in Docs Import as an Edited review source collection;
  5. preview the complete exact overwrite plan and accept the derived-Markdown fidelity warning once; and
  6. apply every edited source to its original canonical collection or none.

The edited Markdown sources are the content authority for this Import. The original JSON/JSONL and trusted export metadata remain authority for provenance, capability, exact prepared membership, routing, and prepared canonical source versions.

Docs Review Build Contract

  • The disabled Built status becomes an enabled Build action whenever one valid package is active and no build request is running.
  • The request freezes only the validated active package_id; it accepts no source path, configured scope, URL fallback, or canonical target.
  • Explicit Build always regenerates the complete package-local projection, even when existing generated JSON is structurally complete.
  • The existing review-specific synthetic configuration and Docs Viewer builder remain the only renderer and compiler.
  • Build reads package-local source/*.md and writes only package-local generated projection. It does not rewrite source front matter, advance the package-local or canonical last_updated, or mutate canonical documents.
  • Success reloads the same package and selected doc. Failure reports the error, stays on the current preview, and re-enables Build for retry.
  • Ordinary reads retain conditional repair: damaged generated output may be repaired, while healthy output is not rebuilt merely by navigation.
  • No watcher registration, source-freshness inference, background rebuild, or per-document incremental build is added.

Edited Review Source Folder Contract

  • The format recognizer runs before generic Markdown-package handling and accepts one staged folder containing the complete set of direct Markdown children materialized by a validated Docs Review package.
  • Every source must have strict canonical front matter and the same review_folder_id, profile, export ID, source scope, and optional source sub-scope. Filename stems and doc_id values must agree and remain unique.
  • Package-local added_date and last_updated remain validated review transport metadata. Editing or building the package does not make either value canonical or eligible to overwrite destination date provenance.
  • Trusted export metadata and the original validated review manifest establish package capability and the exact prepared document set. Missing, extra, duplicate, nested, symlinked, malformed, mixed-package, or cross-collection sources block the folder.
  • A standalone review-source file selected through ordinary Markdown Import is rejected with guidance to stage and select the complete source folder. Its front matter is never rendered as body text.
  • Generic .md files and ordinary one-document Markdown packages retain their current body-oriented create-only behavior.
  • The folder is overwrite-only. Every source doc_id must resolve to exactly one existing { scope, doc_id } or { scope, sub_scope, doc_id } target. There is no create, skip, record selection, title match, or parent fallback.

Dispatch Precedence

The integrated recognizer must receive the untouched staged candidate before ordinary Markdown normalization:

  1. inspect a directory and its unmodified source front matter for one complete edited review package;
  2. accept a valid complete folder into trusted collection planning;
  3. reject an individually selected review source with guidance to stage the complete folder; then
  4. pass only unclaimed ordinary .md files and one-document Markdown packages to the generic normalizer, which may strip a well-formed leading front-matter block before create-only preview.

The generic normalizer may use a scalar title only as an ordinary title fallback. It ignores doc_id, review_*, hierarchy, lifecycle, and status fields and never converts them into overwrite or routing authority.

Canonical Apply Contract

  • Review transport fields, including package-local added_date and last_updated, are validated but never written to canonical front matter.
  • Edited body, title, and summary may replace their canonical counterparts. Immutable doc_id, original added_date, and destination-owned fields such as group, ui_status, and collection configuration remain canonical.
  • Apply compares edited body, title, and summary with the current canonical source through the shared recent-edit comparison. A qualifying change advances canonical last_updated inside the Import mutation boundary; a non-qualifying apply preserves the existing canonical timestamp.
  • Parent and visibility fields apply only where the exact destination collection already permits them. Flat sub-scopes reject hierarchy rather than inventing it.
  • Preview is write-free and shows folder identity, exact collection, document count, all target documents, stale-source state, and the fidelity warning.
  • One explicit confirmation accepts the complete overwrite plan. Prepared canonical versions are revalidated immediately before apply.
  • Apply validates and prepares every write before entering one scope or confined sub-scope mutation boundary. A write or rebuild failure restores the complete pre-apply source snapshot and reports no successful Import.
  • Success refreshes the relevant top-level Docs Viewer state or mounted sub-scope report without changing selection in another surface.

Fidelity Boundary

document-content review source is derived Markdown. Rich content, tokens, comments, raw embeds, source formatting, or package assets may have been lost during rendered conversion. The user owns that acceptance decision by rebuilding and visually inspecting Docs Review before staging the folder.

The Import preview repeats that warning but does not compare with, restore from, or merge content from the original JSON/JSONL package.

Full Document Export Delivery separately proposes exact canonical Markdown and asset/dependency export. ERS-1 does not duplicate that work or make the proposed export-only profile returnable.

Likely Authority

  • The Docs Review controller and provider own Build state, exact active package identity, status, retry, and route-preserving reload.
  • The existing review package service and synthetic builder own explicit regeneration versus conditional read-time repair.
  • The integrated Import format registry owns edited-source-folder recognition before generic Markdown formats.
  • Existing trusted export metadata, returned-package validation, and review manifests own capability, provenance, and exact membership.
  • Shared ImportContent, collection planning, scope/sub-scope target resolution, mutation, rollback, and rebuild owners perform the complete overwrite without a second document parser or mutation model.
  • Scope and report Import controllers reuse one modal, preview, confirmation, busy, retry, and result lifecycle.

Boundary

In scope:

  • explicit complete-package Build in Docs Review;
  • staged edited-review-source-folder discovery and strict validation;
  • one fidelity warning and whole-folder confirmation;
  • overwrite-only exact scope and sub-scope apply;
  • stale-source revalidation, rollback, and appropriate rebuild/refresh;
  • rejection of individual review sources through ordinary Markdown Import; and
  • focused service, module, route, and realistic browser evidence for both destination kinds.

Not in scope:

  • implementing either sub-scope Import prerequisite;
  • editing or regenerating the original returned JSON/JSONL;
  • arbitrary front-matter-aware Markdown Import;
  • creates, partial apply, record selection, moves, deletes, or identity changes;
  • automatic rich-content, token, embed, dependency, or asset restoration;
  • extending docs-watcher; or
  • making document-full-source returnable.

Delivery Tracker

Current state: ERS-1.0 complete. ERS-1.1 is next and remains unstarted.

Review rule: complete one phase, record exact evidence, and stop for review before the next phase.

[x] ERS-1.0 — Confirm Prerequisites And Freeze Authority

  • [x] Confirm ordinary and returned-package Import parity for exact configured sub-scopes, including shared target and rollback seams.
  • [x] Freeze edited Markdown as content authority while retaining trusted package metadata for capability, membership, routing, and staleness.

ERS-1.0 authority and evidence

  • SSO-1 and SRR-2 are closed. Both adopt the shared exact ManagedDocumentCollection; SRR-2 additionally reuses normalized collection planning and the confined sub-scope source-snapshot, write, rollback, and rebuild boundary. There is no parent-scope fallback in those seams.
  • For ERS-1, the selected complete source/ folder owns candidate body, title, summary, and only destination-permitted presentation fields. Trusted export metadata plus the validated Docs Review manifest own capability, profile, export and package identity, exact selected_doc_ids, source scope and optional sub-scope, and prepared source_last_updated values. Review front matter must agree with those authorities but cannot independently grant routing or overwrite permission.
  • Recognition stays in integrated Import before ordinary Markdown normalization. A recognized folder must enter the existing ImportContent and collection-planning model through the frozen exact destination; it does not add a second parser, target resolver, or mutation model.
  • The current sub-scope collection apply is atomic and restores its complete source snapshot plus projection after write or rebuild failure. The current top-level collection apply is not atomic and has no snapshot rollback; ERS-1.3 must add or extend an owned top-level atomic boundary rather than reuse that path unchanged.
  • The existing Docs Review build endpoint validates an exact package_id and uses the synthetic builder, but currently short-circuits when generated output is complete. ERS-1.1 owns changing explicit Build to unconditional regeneration while leaving conditional read-time repair intact.
  • Focused prerequisite and seam evidence passed 46 tests across managed target resolution, collection apply and rollback, and validated review packages. No Build UI, edited-source recognizer, canonical write, or browser workflow was implemented or claimed in ERS-1.0.

Checkpoint / review gate: prerequisites and authority are frozen. Do not begin ERS-1.1 without review.

[ ] ERS-1.1 — Enable Complete Docs Review Build

  • [ ] Make explicit Build run the existing synthetic package builder even when generated output is complete; retain conditional read-time repair.
  • [ ] Add Build busy, success, failure, retry, and route-preserving reload behavior.
  • [ ] Prove Build changes only package-local generated projection and leaves review-source and canonical timestamps untouched.

[ ] ERS-1.2 — Recognize Edited Review Sources

  • [ ] Add the complete-folder recognizer, strict front-matter parsing, shared provenance validation, and individual-file rejection before generic Markdown dispatch.
  • [ ] Prove exact trusted membership and fail closed for unsafe, incomplete, mixed, or non-importable folders.

[ ] ERS-1.3 — Plan And Apply Scope Folders

  • [ ] Map edited sources through the shared normalized collection planner with exact overwrite-only field ownership and stale-source validation.
  • [ ] Ignore review transport dates and use the shared body/title/summary comparison to preserve or advance canonical last_updated during apply.
  • [ ] Apply or restore the complete top-level scope set and refresh the normal Docs Viewer state.

[ ] ERS-1.4 — Apply The Same Contract To Sub-Scopes

  • [ ] Reuse the exact configured sub-scope target, flat collection validation, confined mutation, rollback, rebuild, and report refresh owners.
  • [ ] Prove no parent-scope fallback, discovery rebuild, or cross-collection mutation.

[ ] ERS-1.5 — Verify And Transfer Durable Authority

  • [ ] Exercise realistic scope and Analysis/Tags packages through edit, Build, staged-folder preview, confirmation, apply, and rendered result.
  • [ ] Cover fidelity warning, individual-source rejection, source-version conflicts, rollback, and unchanged generic Markdown/package behavior.
  • [ ] Update Docs Review, Docs Review Endpoints, Docs Import, and exact endpoint/ownership documentation, then rebuild Studio docs and search.

Completion Gate

One scope package and one configured sub-scope package are edited in VS Code, rebuilt and visually accepted in Docs Review, staged as complete source folders, revalidated against their exact prepared and current canonical sets, and applied completely through one shared Import format. Both destinations show the edited content after their appropriate rebuild. Docs Review Build leaves package-local and canonical timestamps untouched; Import advances canonical last_updated exactly when body, title, or summary changed. Generic Markdown, the original JSON/JSONL, unrelated metadata, other collections, and public surfaces remain unchanged.
